rows.reply: Dr. Okafor’s course accepts about 30 to 32 ATP per glucose as the total yield of aerobic respiration. [BIO 201 Lecture 7, p. 1]
The net yield of glycolysis is 2 ATP, 2 NADH, and 2 pyruvate per glucose. [BIO 201 Lecture 7, p. 2]
PFK-1 is the main control point of glycolysis, and it is activated by AMP. [BIO 201 Lecture 7, p. 2]
Thiamine (vitamin B1) deficiency impairs pyruvate dehydrogenase, and the disease is called beriberi. [BIO 201 Lecture 7, p. 3]
Succinate dehydrogenase is the only citric acid cycle enzyme embedded in the inner mitochondrial membrane rather than dissolved in the matrix. [BIO 201 Lecture 7, p. 4]
Each turn of the citric acid cycle produces 3 NADH, 1 FADH2, 1 GTP (converted to ATP), and 2 CO2. [BIO 201 Lecture 7, p. 4]
Uncouplers such as DNP make the inner mitochondrial membrane leaky to protons, so the proton gradient collapses and the energy is released as heat instead of ATP. [BIO 201 Lecture 7, p. 5]
Problem Set 4 is due Friday, October 17 at 11:59 pm on Canvas. [BIO 201 Lecture 7, p. 6]
Dr. Okafor's office hours have moved to Thursday 2–4 pm in Hartley Hall 214. [BIO 201 Lecture 7, p. 6]

Prof. Lindqvist argues that the fiscal crisis was the trigger, not the cause, of the French Revolution, because the deeper causes were structural: the estate system, Enlightenment ideas, and a rising bourgeoisie without political power. [HIST 110 French Revolution notes, Long-term causes]

The Tennis Court Oath was sworn on June 20, 1789, when the deputies met at an indoor tennis court after being locked out of their usual hall. They promised not to separate until France had a constitution. [HIST 110 French Revolution notes, 1789: Estates-General and National Assembly]
Only seven prisoners were inside the Bastille when it was stormed on July 14, 1789. [HIST 110 French Revolution notes, 1789: Estates-General and National Assembly]
Assignats were paper notes issued by the Assembly in 1789 and backed by the nationalized Church lands. [HIST 110 French Revolution notes, Church and money]
The levée en masse of August 1793 conscripted unmarried men aged 18 to 25 and mobilized the whole nation for war. [HIST 110 French Revolution notes, Radical phase and the Terror]
About 17,000 people were officially executed during the Terror. [HIST 110 French Revolution notes, Radical phase and the Terror]
Essay 2 asks whether the Terror was a betrayal or a continuation of the ideals of 1789, and it is due November 21. [HIST 110 French Revolution notes, Course logistics]
Olympe de Gouges answered it in 1791 with the Declaration of the Rights of Woman and of the Female Citizen. [HIST 110 French Revolution notes, Declaration of the Rights of Man and of the Citizen]
Wednesday's chemistry quiz covers buffers only, not titrations. [CHEM 102 buffers lecture recording, 0:00–13:10]
Hydrofluoric acid is the classic trick question because it is weak, even though the other hydrohalic acids are strong. [CHEM 102 buffers lecture recording, 0:00–13:10]
The pH is 4.94, using pH = pKa + log([conjugate base]/[weak acid]) with acetic acid pKa 4.76 and a base-to-acid ratio of 1.5. [CHEM 102 buffers lecture recording, 0:00–13:10]
A buffer works best within plus or minus one pH unit of its pKa. [CHEM 102 buffers lecture recording, 0:00–13:10]
Normal blood pH is held between 7.35 and 7.45. [CHEM 102 buffers lecture recording, 10:40–21:40]

At the half-equivalence point, pH equals pKa because exactly half the acid has been converted to conjugate base, so the base-to-acid ratio is 1 and the log term in Henderson-Hasselbalch is zero. [CHEM 102 buffers lecture recording, 10:40–21:40]
Bring goggles and your pre-lab worksheet; they won’t let you in without both. [CHEM 102 buffers lecture recording, 10:40–21:40]

Buffer pH is the actual pH of the solution, while buffer capacity is how much acid or base the buffer can absorb before the pH changes a lot. [CHEM 102 buffers lecture recording, 10:40–21:40] Capacity depends on the absolute concentrations, so two buffers can have the same pH but different capacities. [CHEM 102 buffers lecture recording, 10:40–21:40]
In the latte example, the price elasticity of demand was 1, so demand was unit elastic. [EconExplained: price elasticity (YouTube), 0:00–4:37]

We use the midpoint method because the simple percentage formula gives a different elasticity depending on whether price goes up or down. The midpoint method fixes this by calculating the percentage change using the average of the starting and ending values, so the result is the same either way. [EconExplained: price elasticity (YouTube), 0:00–4:37]
If demand is elastic, a price cut raises total revenue because quantity rises by a bigger percentage than price falls. [EconExplained: price elasticity (YouTube), 0:00–4:37]

The four determinants are: availability of close substitutes, necessities versus luxuries, the share of your budget, and time horizon. The video says more substitutes make demand more elastic, necessities tend to be inelastic while luxuries tend to be elastic, smaller budget shares tend to be inelastic, and demand gets more elastic over time. [EconExplained: price elasticity (YouTube), 0:00–4:37] [EconExplained: price elasticity (YouTube), 4:07–7:15]
If cross-price elasticity is negative, the goods are complements, like printers and ink cartridges. [EconExplained: price elasticity (YouTube), 4:07–7:15]
The video gives instant ramen for a lot of students as an example of an inferior good. [EconExplained: price elasticity (YouTube), 4:07–7:15]
The elasticity is 2.5, so demand is elastic, and the venue should lower prices to increase revenue. [EconExplained: price elasticity (YouTube), 4:07–7:15]

No—elasticity is not the same as slope. Along a straight-line demand curve, elasticity changes: demand is elastic at the top and inelastic at the bottom. [EconExplained: price elasticity (YouTube), 4:07–7:15]

The episodic buffer was added to the working memory model by Baddeley in 2000. [PSYC 100 memory study guide, Working memory (Baddeley and Hitch, 1974)]
Patient H.M. could still learn new motor skills like mirror drawing after his surgery, even though he could not form new explicit long-term memories. [PSYC 100 memory study guide, Long-term memory]
A 30-second distraction task before recall wipes out the recency effect but leaves primacy intact. [PSYC 100 memory study guide, Serial position effect]
Retroactive interference is when new information disrupts recall of old information, like your new phone number making you forget the old one. [PSYC 100 memory study guide, Forgetting]
